Subject: Renewal uplift — mid-year capacity add and invoice smoothing

Hi Ben,

Hope you're well. We're kicking off our renewal discussions and have a mid-year usage spike coming (expected +55% token volume in Q4 due to a pilot launch). Procurement asked whether we can: 1) provision an interim capacity uplift for 6 months, 2) have that uplift co-term with our existing renewal on 2028-10-01, and 3) smooth/prorate billing so the Q4 spend doesn't blow the budget line items.

Attached is our current SOW and recent usage export (Orchid_SOW_v3.pdf, usage_history_q2.csv). High level asks:
- Temporary uplift = 120M tokens/month for Oct–Mar
- Prefer to avoid a separate invoice cadence (one consolidated invoice is better)
- Looking for guidance on discounting for committed short-term top-ups and any incentives to co-term to 10/01/2028

Can you put together 2–3 options we can take to procurement this week? We have an internal steering meeting on Wednesday, 8/22.

Thanks — Harper
Harper Li
Head of Product Operations | Orchid Health

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Renewal uplift — mid-year capacity add and invoice smoothing

Harper — thanks for the context and for sending the SOW. Appreciate the heads-up on the Q4 pilot.

Quick summary of options we can offer procurement (brief, so you can share quickly):

Option 1 — Temporary Top-up (no change to contract term)
- Add a 6-month uplift of 120M tokens/mo (Oct–Mar) billed monthly
- No long-term commitment; unit price = hosted on-demand rate with a 6% volume discount for the uplift portion
- Separate line item on invoices (clean accounting)

Option 2 — Hybrid Top-up + Co-term (recommended for predictability)
- Convert uplift into a temporary committed add-on that co-terms to 2028-10-01
- 6-month uplift amortized across the remainder of the contract so invoices remain consolidated
- Effective discount on the uplift portion = 12% (reflects partial annualization + commit)
- We can include a one-time procurement credit of $7,500 if PO signed by 8/31

Option 3 — Annualize and Annual Discount (best unit economics)
- Annualize the uplift into a 12-month commitment starting 10/01 (moves to a new committed seat/bucket)
- Discount = 18% on uplift volume; requires annual billing and a revised SLA addendum

Open items I noted for our side: legal approval on SLA carveouts for the pilot load, precise invoicing format you need for budget lines, and whether Orchid prefers a single consolidated invoice vs. line-item split.

If you want, I can draft procurement-friendly language and a short mutual action plan for Wednesday's steering meeting. Looping in Irene (legal) to flag SLA/term considerations.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Irene / Lauren — quick ask: Orchid Health is evaluating a 6-month uplift (120M tokens/mo) and prefers co-terming to 2028-10-01 with consolidated invoicing. I proposed three options (temp top-up, hybrid co-term amortized, and annualize).

Questions: 1) legal: any SLA carveouts or language we should avoid for a short-term hybrid that amortizes across the contract? 2) finance: is the proposed $7.5k procurement credit (one-time) ok to approve at AE level or do we need a formal discount approval? 3) invoicing: is there a recommended way to amortize an uplift across the renewal period while keeping a single invoice?

They want options for procurement by Wed 8/22. Can you review and I’ll fold notes into the draft M.A.P.

—Ben

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Aug 2028 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Internal — need quick legal + finance guidance on Orchid uplift options

Ben — tagging in quick guidance.

Legal notes:
- Hybrid amortization model is fine but avoid language that implies the uplift creates a permanent quota change until Orchid signs a formal amendment. Suggest "temporary committed add-on" language with explicit start/end dates and an automatic revert clause.
- SLA carveouts: for pilot-related surge, we can provide a limited SLA exception for burst capacity (performance best-effort) but keep incident reporting and audit logs unchanged. Any exception should expire at uplift end date.

Finance notes (cc Lauren):
- Lauren: confirm whether AE can approve a $7.5k credit. If not, provide the approval path and expected turnaround.
- On amortization: finance prefers a single invoice with two line items (base and uplift amortized) and an accompanying invoice memo explaining the amortization schedule. That avoids multiple invoice numbers while preserving accounting clarity.

Irene
Irene Choi
Head of Legal | Redwood Inference

From: Marta Ruiz <m.ruiz@orchidhealth.com>

Ben / Irene — thanks for the quick turnaround and clarity. Procurement likes Option 2 (Hybrid Top-up + Co-term) because it keeps invoicing simple and gives predictable unit economics. A few notes from our side:

- We will request the $7,500 procurement credit be reflected as a line-item credit on the first co-term invoice.
- Orchids' finance needs the amortization schedule in CSV format (line item per month) for our ERP. Can you provide that?
- We also need the co-term amendment (language per Irene's suggestions) and the limited SLA exception text to send to our security and compliance teams.

If you can provide the M.A.P., the amortization CSV, and the amendment draft today, we can get a PO to you by 8/31. Procurement emphasized that if the PO is received by 8/31 we should get the procurement credit.

I'll mark the steering meeting as a short decision item.

Best,
Marta Ruiz
